correctness.rationale: For each lowest-common-ancestor split (a,b), Kendall loss optimizes its two block orders independently, giving D(T)=sum_v g(a_v,b_v). The singleton interleaving yields F_m; the without-replacement inversion variance ab(a+b+1)/12 and Cauchy-Schwarz imply g(a,b)>=ab/4 away from five small explicitly evaluated cases. Harmonic-sum comparison bounds F_{a+b}-F_a-F_b<=ab/4-1/6, equality only (2,2), while singleton splits have zero surcharge. Telescoping over all nodes proves caterpillar uniqueness and sharp exactly-one-balanced-four-leaf-core runner-up for every m>=4. Independent exact interleaving enumeration through total size 12 checked surcharges; finite tests are not the infinite proof.
